output.brief: Don't discipline drivers or retrain everyone yet. The evidence points away from driver technique, the hills and the new pads. It points to the brake work done at Northfield Motor Services while the Eastgate bay was closed. All 11 vans with soft-pedal complaints were serviced there. Northfield also serviced two more vans, which are not in the complaint list. Calder Road Garage fitted the same pads in the same period, and no Calder van shows up. Every Eastgate van ran Upper Wend on 9 to 16 days. The same drivers logged 141 Upper Wend days in non-Northfield vans with no brake reports. Reports were zero in July and August, after the reporting app launched, so easier reporting doesn't explain it. I'm fairly confident, but I haven't seen the Northfield job cards or fluid tests, so the exact fault (probably the brake fluid) is inferred. Next: pull the Northfield-serviced vans from service, boiling-point test the fluid and renew it from sealed stock, and check the two Northfield vans with no complaints. Ask Northfield for their fluid records. Protect the people who reported faults. Leave the pad supplier alone until squeal is checked against fresh pads of the old brand.
